scope.kind: Architecture reassessment only; CPU reads and arithmetic on pinned source and archived local artifacts. No implementation, model reload, GPU, SSH, process signalling, installs, weight download, application termination, source edits or commits.
scope.small_policy_audit: Not duplicated; independently delegated to another reviewer.
scope.optional_external_check: An optional pinned raw-GitHub extraction was attempted; configured extract backend returned search-only/unsupported. All technical conclusions below use the verified local pin, not missing web content.

decision.recommendation: STOP full27B RPC admission and all further full-load retries under the unchanged deployment constraints. Bounded transport work may be retained as a separate CPU-first experiment, not as a demonstrated route to target fit.
decision.reason: Bounded weight messages can remove a real near-1GiB transient per host at output-head upload, but that upload already completed. V3 later hit laptop warning pressure after only4.629GiB of6.261GiB raw remote weights, with1.631GiB still missing and caches/workspaces uninitialized. A short-lived buffer optimization has no proven multi-GiB steady-state saving. The exact capacity shortfall cannot be calculated from these telemetry fields.
decision.status: All three full-target attempts remain failed/not admitted; no ready full27B model, completion, image answer, performance qualification or always-on admission.
decision.native_MLX_baseline: A different-format native4bit MLX baseline is separate evidence; this review neither requalifies it nor substitutes it for exact-GGUF comparison.

identity_and_inventory.identity_scope: Whole-file digests come from the retained completed provisioning readback and v3 admitted config, not a new remote hash. No full weight files are available locally for this audit.
identity_and_inventory.placement: Same3,2 split: mini blocks0..39, laptop blocks40..63 plus output_norm/head; input embedding on mini CPU; unused prediction block64 excluded. Printed offloaded66/66 is not66 executed decoder blocks.

The trace allocation line is rounded, so page-rounded size is source-derived, not an independently printed exact allocation result.

v3_upload_accounting.method: Parse only receiver [set_tensor] records, match names/types/shapes to independently reparsed header inventory, sum exact header tensor bytes (not rounded trace sizes). Validate every observed offset is0 and receiver data addresses form a gap-free buffer prefix. Match FNV request values between client/server logs. Do not count client intent or hash request as an uploaded payload.
v3_upload_accounting.coverage: Head+norm, every remote tensor in blocks40..56, and11/14 tensors of block57. Block57 three FFN matrices and every tensor in blocks58..63 are missing.

head.name: output.weight
head.arrival_assurance: Receiver trace shows full-frame receive returned before set_tensor logs. It then advances through later commands, so the shared memcpy and case-local vector destruction completed. Send-return is socket-send completion, not by itself a receiver ACK. No per-tensor byte readback was recorded.

unuploaded_client_intent.name: blk.57.ffn_gate.weight
unuploaded_client_intent.reason: Only the next SET_TENSOR_HASH request begins at55.063019s and fails on controlled peer closure; no corresponding receiver payload exists. Exclude this61,276,160byte tensor from uploaded totals.

v3_upload_accounting.digest_limits: FNV1a64 values are sender-computed cache lookup keys merely echoed by server cache-miss logging, not receiver-computed payload digests or collision-resistant integrity proofs. No receiver SHA256/get_tensor readback was captured for v3 weights.102 request keys match across logs;137 smaller received tensors have no recorded per-tensor key. Whole-file/header/log SHA256 identities and matching metadata are stronger provenance, but not a replacement for end-to-end tensor readback.

telemetry.source: results/full-target-load-v3/local-result.json, ssh-readback/result.json; all counters belong to their explicitly selected host/PID. Global fields are not exclusively attributable to RPC.
telemetry.sampled_progression: At31.798s RPC footprint is42.6MB. At33.889s it is2.073GiB, free715MiB. At38.185s footprint2.893GiB/free60MiB. At46.691s footprint4.286GiB and physical compressor0.836GiB. At48.787s RSS falls to0.457GiB while footprint rises to4.679GiB and global compressor reaches5.300GiB. At55.214s pressure2, footprint5.765GiB, RSS1.207GiB and free47.06MiB. RSS collapse is not successful weight reclamation.
telemetry.v2_contrast: v2 default residency produced an archived global wired increase6,727,483,392bytes (~6.265GiB), pressure2 after29.579s and only20KiB receiver upload. v3 removes that eager-wired signature, not final capacity demand: wired rises only15,269,888bytes between first and warning samples, while anonymous/compressor demand grows during upload.
telemetry.mini: Mini pressure remains1 throughout; maximum sampled RSS9.919662GiB, then falls as mapped pages transition/reclaim. No mini footprint/global counters were captured in v3, and RSS does not bound driver or whole-host residency. Projector/cache/compute readiness was not reached.
telemetry.footprint_limits: No hard process phys_footprint/jetsam budget or per-region/allocator attribution was recorded. Reported phys_footprint_peak is a high-water field, not a limit. v2 low process footprint coexisted with multi-GiB global wiring; v3 low RSS coexisted with high footprint/compressor. None of RSS, phys_footprint or advertised backend free bytes alone bounds total OS/GPU residency.

residual_observation.interpretation: Approximate diagnostic residual, not a synchronized allocation decomposition. Near1GiB excess could include allocator/VM accounting retention, backend/driver/bookkeeping or other live allocations. It does NOT establish a retained std::vector or a persistent head leak. Source proves vector object destruction at each SET_TENSOR break. A per-region allocation trace or bounded A/B is needed.

telemetry.sampling_limits: ~2s sequential samples are not instantaneous peaks or per-frame timestamps. Client relative log clock is separate from controller timestamps; no precise cross-host clock alignment is assumed. Global compression can involve unrelated processes. Swapouts unchanged does not imply healthy pressure.

client_serialization.finding: serialize_set_tensor allocates zero-initialized new uint8_t[305+payload] and memcpy-copies the whole requested span. Source/mmap pages coexist with this owned staging allocation. shared_ptr ownership retains those bytes through dispatcher send; this is a real model-sized per-frame temporary in the mini, not a pointer-only header.

receiver_frame.finding: recv_msg resizes one local vector to the whole message before socket receive. That vector is created INSIDE the SET_TENSOR case and destroyed on break. set_tensor synchronizes backends, parses header+offset, validates region, and synchronously sets bytes. There is no persistent vector-capacity bank in this case. Freed allocation may or may not remain charged by libc/VM; source alone cannot answer that.

metal_shared.finding: Actual v3 startup confirms use_shared_buffers=true, use_residency_sets=false. Shared destination is a page-aligned vm_allocate allocation wrapped in newBufferWithBytesNoCopy. No source-visible second full-shard CPU-to-GPU copy is allocated. Shared set_tensor is immediate memcpy into destination+offset. Without explicit residency, allocation is not an explicit all-pages memset; actual first writes still materialize weights.

metal_private_alternative.finding: Private allocation reserves GPU storage and wraps source bytes in a temporary shared MTLBuffer for blit, waiting on completion before releasing source wrapper. It is not a demonstrated lower-memory alternative on unified RAM. It adds driver/copy/lifetime complexity and changes the buffer-policy variable already held fixed; reject a blind private-buffer retry.

mmap_remote_boundary.finding: RPC reports buffer_from_host_ptr=false: mini mmap cannot become laptop zero-copy destination. Current mmap loading calls synchronous whole-tensor ggml_backend_tensor_set. Existing four1MiB asynchronous file-upload staging buffers are bypassed with mmap, and RPC caps.host_buffer=false also defeats that fast path. Simply flipping mmap off is not a proven bounded-upload solution.

socket_chunk_is_not_frame_bound.finding: MAX_CHUNK_SIZE=1GiB caps individual send/recv syscall spans, not message size or staging allocation. Lowering it alone leaves both whole-frame client and receiver allocations unchanged.

queue.finding: Dispatcher std::queue has no item/byte cap and send_async can accumulate owning serialized inputs. That is a real unbounded API surface, but not demonstrated causation here: mmap weights use the synchronous setter and one serial loader producer. send waits for socket-send completion, not receiver acknowledgment; bounded TCP buffers can overlap adjacent frames, and a transient old shared_ptr can overlap the next serialization. Receiver processes one SET_TENSOR vector at a time, with no queue of full weight frames. No evidence of an unbounded v3 weight pipeline. Preserve explicit byte credits and construction budget if adding async chunking.

safe_partial_set.finding: Existing SET_TENSOR has byte offset and byte-span semantics: same tensor metadata, source pointer+chunk_start, offset=original_offset+chunk_start, size=min(C,remaining). GGML checks tensor bound; receiver checks backing buffer and shared Metal memcpy honors offset. Packed bytes need no requantization/kernel change; choose bounded valid spans, preferably block-aligned, then prove complete bytes and unchanged surrounding regions. No protocol redesign is necessary for a CPU-first chunked-caller proof.
safe_partial_set.safety_caveats: Existing out-of-bounds checks are asserts/buffer checks, not hardened hostile-input admission. Future frame cap must check length BEFORE vector.resize and use overflow-safe subtraction before pointer arithmetic. Current handler allocates announced length before header validation. Validate original offset<=tensor bytes and length<=remaining; refuse truncated/oversized/overlapping incomplete transactions at higher-level admission. SET is fire-and-forget; GET reply gives a receiver-processed fence.

cache.finding: Server cache is disabled (local cache n/a), but sender still hashes weight spans>10MiB and sends lookup requests; all102 observed are misses. Chunking at1MiB bypasses the threshold and removes whole-head FNV scan on this no-cache path, but do not mix speed claims with memory. Cache-enabled mode is separate: cached_file vectors are whole cache-entry size; using an old whole-head cache hit before chunking would retain the giant-buffer risk. Freeze cache off for minimal A/B, then test chunk-key offset/length/cache-hit behavior independently before broader adoption.

saving_scale_and_capacity.benefit_scope: About993.63MiB less maximum application-owned staging per host at the head (not pooled across hosts); destination weights are unchanged. This bounds live frame allocations, not a promised physical-footprint saving. Head already completed in v3. Largest other laptop tensor is69.73MiB; largest actually received later tensor58.44MiB, so later per-frame savings are at most57.44MiB versus1MiB chunks. End-of-trace ssm_out is20.625MiB, not a1GiB live head frame.
saving_scale_and_capacity.destination_policy_limit: Per-tensor or deferred buffer reservation could change VM/residency bookkeeping but v3 has no giant eager-wired increase left to remove. All6.261GiB destination weight bytes are still required. Reclaiming/freeing uploaded tensors changes model residency/streaming architecture, not ordinary buffer allocation. Remote mmap/file-backed weights need a different verified asset/storage architecture, not a message-size flag.
saving_scale_and_capacity.headroom_evidence: 16GiB physical memory is archived for the laptop. Just before writes it had~2.78GiB free pages, then47MiB by warning, with5.56GiB new physical compressor occupancy. Historical system footprint is21.006GiB laptop and6.409GiB mini; these ledgers are not directly subtractable from physical RAM. Advertised~11.84GiB backend free comes from recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize-currentAllocatedSize (ggml-metal-device.m:1501-1506), not allocatable OS headroom. Runtime allowances are planning reserves, not measured requirements or a proven hard4.069GiB shortfall.
saving_scale_and_capacity.judgment: Removing a potential0.970GiB head temporary/retention would still be smaller than1.631GiB unuploaded raw weights, before estimated2.438GiB laptop runtime buffers; the mini also has an unqualified12.166GiB estimated stack before OS/apps. This is not a mathematical impossibility proof because reclaimability/accounting overlap and actual workspace are unknown. It is insufficient evidence to authorize another full load or claim chunking fixes capacity.

goals: Bind immutable source/checkpoint/header/placement and readback SHA256 identities.
Compare stock whole-span and chunked uploads using identical tensor type/shape/stride/storage bytes; no weight or kernel change.
For each tensor verify contiguous coverage[0,nbytes), unique offsets, exact final short chunk and expected digest; no missing/duplicate/out-of-range bytes.
Read back in bounded GET slices AFTER receiver-processed fence, compute receiver SHA256 incrementally, compare every byte against source and stock control; do not accept FNV cache keys as integrity.
Verify nonzero base offsets, views where supported, guard bytes untouched, unaligned logical tails, quantization-block boundaries and multiple tensor boundaries.

Test0,1,C-1,C,C+1,2C+tail payload sizes, short reads/fragmented headers and data, disconnect during chunk, oversized lengths and overflow at local parser boundary. Failed transaction cannot publish loaded/admitted state.
Freeze cache disabled for initial gate; separately test hash-hit/miss, chunk offset+length binding and refusal of a cached oversized whole tensor.
Under async variants prove a finite outstanding-byte cap includes buffers being constructed and queued, not just sent frames; test producer outrunning blocked receiver and cancellation cleanup.
Only after CPU transport equality and later owner-approved small physical shared-Metal parity may full-model capacity be reassessed. Neither test is27B inference or a workload qualification.

minimal_AB_probe_proposal.purpose: One bounded transport/offset lifetime discriminator, never another model reload. CPU-only pinned-library/socket fixture first; no Metal device enumeration or kernel work. A later physical shared-Metal version requires explicit hardware-owner authorization and separate admission.
minimal_AB_probe_proposal.tensor: One contiguous F32 raw-byte tensor, no arithmetic, total allocation N+128bytes. Initial fill0xA5;64byte guards before/after an N-byte region. Set region at original byte offset64. F32 is only storage; transport equality is not numerical admission.
minimal_AB_probe_proposal.source: Same fixed deterministic high-entropy counter-hash byte pattern in A/B; record seed and source SHA256. Allocate one source buffer only; compute expected/readback digests incrementally rather than another full tensor copy.
minimal_AB_probe_proposal.A: Fresh CPU-only fixture process/connection, cache disabled, identical destination policy. One existing ggml_backend_tensor_set(tensor,source,64,N). Read a small GET at the end as receiver fence; then bounded64KiB whole-tensor readback with exact guard and byte equality.
minimal_AB_probe_proposal.B: Fresh otherwise identical fixture: repeat existing setter with offsets64+j and source+j; chunk size1,048,576bytes,8 full chunks+256byte tail. A receiver-processed small GET fence after each chunk forces at most one in-flight application payload and makes temp destruction observable. Same final bounded readback.

memory_cap.scope: Conservative source+destination+client-frame+receiver-frame+two64KiB readback blocks:32.127MiB. Baseline libraries/interpreter, allocator overhead, socket buffers and OS/driver accounting are separate; do not promise total RSS<64MiB. Enforce a fixture allocation ledger below64MiB and abort rather than inflate any requested buffer. If the user means total process footprint<64MiB, admit actual baseline first and reduce N to1MiB+256 if necessary.

record: source/binary hashes, exact sent/received byte counts and tensor metadata
frame live-size/allocation high-water using fixture instrumentation at allocate/receive/set/destroy boundaries, not only2s polling
per-process footprint/RSS before, after receiver fence, after free and0.1/0.5/2s later if physical version is authorized; global wired/compressor/pressure separately
final receiver SHA256, stock-vs-chunk bytes, sentinel guards, offset and tail coverage
bounded deadline<=30s, logs<=8MiB, no resident service, exact owned-process/listener cleanup; physical variant normal-pressure guard unchanged

expected_architectural_signal.retention_hypothesis: If post-fence footprint stays proportional to the largest A frame but not B, allocator/VM retention is supported at this small size; source-object lifetime still ends at break. If both return to baseline but B peaks lower, benefit is transient only. If destination growth dominates equally, chunking does not reduce steady demand.

minimal_AB_probe_proposal.limitations: N is below the10MiB hash threshold, intentionally isolating offset/frame behavior. It cannot reproduce the full head hash scan/cache path or1GiB allocator regime. Negative/parser/cache tests are separate bounded CPU gates. A successful8MiB fixture cannot establish multi-GiB fit, actual Metal residency or model numerical correctness. No hardware test was executed in this reassessment.

failures_interpretation: In all3 trials the local pressure guard deliberately terminates only its owned RPC worker (exit-15); the mini later aborts at the RPC assertion on peer closure (exit-6). The generic Remote RPC server crashed/malformed message is a consequence, not evidence of an independent spontaneous RPC crash.
